subject: Env readiness playbook + exception escalation ladder for private/VPC deployments
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.example.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com, marcus_lin@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Cc: greenbank-security@greenbank.com
Date: 2028-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Env readiness playbook + exception escalation ladder for private/VPC deployments

Team —

Following up from last week's sync with Greenbank: they have committed to a pilot for our VPC-hosted private deployment but several key items need cross-functional decisions before we can schedule provisioning. I attached a first-pass playbook and a proposed escalation ladder for exceptions. High-level asks: 

1) Architecture: can the runtime team confirm the minimum infra footprint (GPU types, node counts, storage IOPS) for a 3-node pilot handling ~50 qps steady-state with short tail latency SLO (p95 < 120ms)? Add tolerances for batch size 8.

2) Security/compliance gaps: Greenbank's security team flagged audit-logging latency and key rotation procedures. Need an owner from security to confirm whether our current KMS integration and audit-log exports meet their needs or whether we need an exception lane.

3) Resourcing & oncall: Marcus, we need an estimate for implementation effort (Dev + SRE) and an oncall runway for pilot week 0-4. If this requires a dedicated oncall, note the cost and whether we can use a shared pager rotation.

4) Exceptions: if the pilot requires nonstandard network changes (e.g. dedicated transit between customer DC and our edge), we'll need an internal exception and an exec sign-off path. Please review the attached ladder and propose edits.

Can each of you reply with concrete answers (or owner assignments) by EOD Tuesday 6/22 so Marissa can finalize the pilot gating criteria for the Monday steering review?

Attachments: private-deploy-playbook_v1.xlsx, escalation-ladder_v1.pdf

Thanks —
Soojin Lee
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.example.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.example.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com, marcus_lin@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com

Subject: Re: Env readiness playbook + exception escalation ladder for private/VPC deployments

On 2028-06-21 09:12, Soojin Lee wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Following up from last week's sync with Greenbank: they have committed to a pilot for our VPC-hosted private deployment but several key items need cross-functional decisions before we can schedule provisioning.

Short answers / technical constraints below:

- Minimum infra for pilot: with current runtime we recommend 3x a40-equivalent nodes (NVIDIA A40 or spot-equivalent) with 1.2TB NVMe per node and a shared 20k IOPS network-attached cache for KV. This supports ~50 qps with batching (8) and p95 ~110ms in our lab runs.

- Storage/IOPS: if Greenbank will run long context lengths (>8k tokens), we need to expand NVMe and increase network IOPS — this materially changes cost.

- Network: we can support transit peering, but we'll need a private peering link and BGP configuration. That requires a network runbook and 48-72h lead time with the colo/vendor (Acme Cloud).

- KMS/key rotation: we support customer-managed keys via KMS; rotation is currently weekly but rotation-handshake logging is batched — audit export delay is up to 15 minutes. If Greenbank requires sub-minute audit pushing we will need a new streaming export path.

I've attached a rough capacity projection for the recommended pilot (capacity-projection.csv). Action items:
- Marcus: confirm SRE headcount to do BGP + peering validation and 24/7 pilot support.
- Grace: can you confirm compliance owner to triage KMS/audit export SLA?

If we proceed with the above config, provisioning lead time is ~3 weeks (vendor procurement + network), or ~1 week if we can use an existing peering arrangement with Acme Cloud.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Staff Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.example.com, dev_patel@redwood.example.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: 2028-06-22T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Env readiness playbook + exception escalation ladder for private/VPC deployments

Appreciate the clear asks. Two things from SRE/ops perspective:

1) Resourcing: for a 3-week pilot window + 4 weeks of run support we estimate 2 FTEs (one SRE + one Network Engineer) dedicated during provisioning week and a shared oncall rotation (0.25 FTE equiv) for steady state. If Greenbank requires a dedicated pager, add +1 FTE for triage. Rough labor cost estimate attached.

2) Exception ladder: the attached escalation-ladder_v1.pdf looks fine functionally but the timing windows are optimistic. We recommend adding an intermediate tier: "Network Remediation (24h)" before escalating to EVP for sign-off.

Trade-offs: if we reduce accelerator spec to cheaper GPUs (e.g., A10 instead of A40) we can cut infra cost ~30% but expect p95 to worsen ~15-25ms. Recommend we run a short perf validation (2 days) on A10s to quantify impact before committing.

Related ask: procurement needs a formal statement of work and PO path. Marissa — can you confirm whether we should treat this under the existing Greenbank MSA (preferred) or run a separate SOW? That decision changes the contract timeline.

Attachments: capacity-projection.csv

Marcus Lin
Director, Site Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.example.com, dev_patel@redwood.example.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com, marcus_lin@redwood.example.com
Date: 2028-06-22T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Env readiness playbook + exception escalation ladder for private/VPC deployments

Thanks everyone — good progress. Quick decisions/next steps: 

- Approve pilot configuration as described by Dev (3x A40-equivalent nodes, NVMe, shared cache). Dev/Marcus to run the 48h perf validation on A10s and report delta by 6/28.
- Compliance: Grace to own KMS/audit export SLA negotiation with Greenbank; confirm whether the existing KMS rotation cadence is acceptable or if we need streaming export by 6/26.
- Procurement/SOW: Use existing Greenbank MSA; we will add an SOW amendment for pilot scope to avoid new legal lanes. I'll loop in procurement after this thread.
- Oncall: Marcus to provide final FTE ask by 6/24. If >=1 dedicated FTE is required, I need an explicit justification for capacity planning.
- Exceptions: Soojin, update the escalation ladder with Marcus's intermediate tier and assign owners for each step; we'll use that as the formal exception path if network peering or audit streaming is required.

I've scheduled a short decision review on 6/23 at 10:00 PT — link below. Please come prepared with the perf numbers and a procurement timeline.

Meeting link: https://redwood.app/meetings/soojin/2028-06-23
